questions.question_text: An element has the valence-shell configuration ns²np¹. Which block contains it?
questions.explanation: A differentiating electron entering a p subshell places the element in the p block; ns²np¹ is a common group 13 configuration.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The last electron of an element enters a d subshell. In which broad region of the periodic table should it be placed?
questions.explanation: The periodic-table block is named for the subshell into which the differentiating electron enters; d-block elements occupy the central region.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The lanthanoids and actinoids are placed separately below the main body of the periodic table because their differentiating electrons enter the
questions.explanation: These inner-transition series involve filling of f orbitals and are shown separately to keep the table compact.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which element is placed in group 18 despite having an s² configuration rather than an ns²np⁶ valence configuration?
questions.explanation: Helium has a filled 1s² shell; its complete outer shell and chemical inertness place it with the noble gases.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Hydrogen resembles both alkali metals and halogens in different chemical behaviours. This is why its position in the periodic table is often described as
questions.explanation: Hydrogen has one valence electron but also needs one electron to complete its shell, so it shows analogies with group 1 and group 17 and is often treated uniquely.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which element is a metalloid commonly used as a semiconductor in electronic devices?
questions.explanation: Silicon is a metalloid and an important semiconductor; germanium is another familiar example.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Across a period, the first ionisation energy generally tends to increase because
questions.option_a: effective nuclear attraction on outer electrons tends to increase
questions.option_b: the number of occupied shells increases at every step
questions.option_d: outer electrons become farther from the nucleus in every element
questions.explanation: Across a period, nuclear charge rises while added electrons enter the same main shell, so effective attraction generally increases; small exceptions occur.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is the first ionisation energy of a noble gas generally high?
questions.option_a: Its occupied outer shell is relatively stable, so removing an electron requires substantial energy
questions.option_c: Its electrons are all in the nucleus
questions.option_d: It readily forms positive ions in water
questions.explanation: Noble gases have stable closed-shell configurations, making electron removal energetically unfavourable compared with many neighbouring elements.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the general trend in metallic character from left to right across a period?
questions.option_a: It generally decreases as atoms hold valence electrons more strongly
questions.option_c: It is identical for every element
questions.explanation: Increasing effective nuclear attraction across a period makes electron loss less favourable, so metallic character generally decreases.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which property generally increases down a group for elements with comparable outer-electron patterns?
questions.option_d: The valence shell moving closer to the nucleus
questions.explanation: Each step down a group adds occupied inner shells, increasing shielding of the valence electrons from the nucleus.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Halogens become less reactive as oxidising agents down group 17 largely because
questions.option_a: larger atoms attract an additional electron less strongly
questions.option_b: their proton number falls to zero
questions.option_c: they lose all valence electrons more easily
questions.explanation: Down the group, increased size and shielding reduce the attraction for an incoming electron, so oxidising ability generally decreases.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Transition elements often show variable oxidation states because
questions.option_a: the energies of their outer ns and inner (n−1)d electrons can be similar
questions.option_c: their nuclei change charge in chemical reactions
questions.explanation: Both ns and (n−1)d electrons may participate in bonding, allowing several oxidation states in many transition elements.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Many transition-metal ions are coloured, whereas most s-block ions are colourless. A common reason is that transition-metal ions can have
questions.option_a: partly filled d orbitals that absorb visible light
questions.option_d: nuclei that emit all visible colours
questions.explanation: Partially filled d orbitals can permit electronic transitions that absorb portions of visible light, giving many transition-metal ions colour.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which feature makes many transition metals useful as catalysts?
questions.option_a: They can adopt variable oxidation states and provide surfaces for reactants
questions.option_d: They are all gases at room temperature
questions.explanation: Variable oxidation states and adsorption on metal surfaces can provide alternative pathways that speed up reactions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement about the actinoid series is correct?
questions.option_a: It is an inner-transition series, and many members are radioactive
questions.option_b: It consists only of stable noble gases
questions.explanation: Actinoids are f-block inner-transition elements; all are radioactive, though their half-lives vary widely.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which neutral atom has the electron configuration 2,8,7 and therefore is chlorine?
questions.explanation: A neutral atom with 2 + 8 + 7 = 17 electrons has atomic number 17, corresponding to chlorine.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A neutral atom has the configuration 2,8,2. Which simple ion is it most likely to form to reach a stable noble-gas configuration?
questions.explanation: An atom with two outer electrons can lose them to form a stable 2+ ion; magnesium (2,8,2) is a common example.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An element forms a 3− ion and has a stable octet after gaining three electrons. How many valence electrons did its neutral atom have?
questions.explanation: An atom that gains three electrons to complete an octet begins with five valence electrons, typical of group 15 main-group elements.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pair of elements is most likely to have similar chemical properties because their atoms have analogous outer-shell configurations?
questions.explanation: Lithium and sodium are in the same main-group family and have one valence electron, giving them similar chemical behaviour.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which period contains only two elements?
questions.explanation: The first period contains hydrogen and helium; it is the shortest period.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which element has the highest electronegativity on the Pauling scale among the following?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element on the Pauling scale, strongly attracting shared electrons in a bond.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pair correctly identifies the main-group family names for groups 2 and 16, respectively?
questions.explanation: Group 2 elements are alkaline earth metals; group 16 elements are commonly called chalcogens.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which noble gas is commonly used in illuminated advertising signs because an electric discharge produces a bright reddish-orange glow?
questions.explanation: Neon signs emit a characteristic reddish-orange light when an electric discharge passes through the gas; other colours can use different gases or coatings.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement about noble-gas atoms is most accurate under ordinary conditions?
questions.option_a: They are generally monatomic and have low chemical reactivity
questions.option_b: They all exist as diatomic molecules
questions.option_c: They readily form salts with every metal
questions.option_d: They have incomplete outer shells except helium
questions.explanation: Noble gases are generally monatomic and relatively unreactive because of stable outer-shell configurations; heavier members can form compounds under special conditions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which change generally occurs when a neutral atom forms a positive ion?
questions.option_a: It loses one or more electrons
questions.option_b: It gains one or more electrons
questions.option_c: Its proton number changes in an ordinary chemical reaction
questions.explanation: A cation forms when electrons are removed; the nucleus and atomic number do not change in ordinary ion formation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An anion is often larger than its neutral parent atom because adding electrons increases
questions.option_a: electron-electron repulsion within the valence shell
questions.option_b: the number of protons in the nucleus
questions.option_c: the nuclear charge by one for every electron
questions.option_d: the mass number by the number of shells
questions.explanation: When electrons are added without changing proton number, increased electron-electron repulsion can expand the electron cloud.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: How many elements are present in the fourth period of the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: The fourth period has 18 elements as the 4s, 3d and 4p subshells are filled in sequence.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which period is the first to include the f-block elements in its full length?
questions.explanation: The sixth period includes the lanthanoid series in the f block, making it the first period with f-block elements.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: How many vertical groups are present in the modern long-form periodic table?
questions.explanation: The modern long-form periodic table has 18 vertical groups.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Chemistry, Classification of Elements and Periodicity, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
